## Decision and cutoff

The common head of this **draft PR remains `bf42d2a5c2c1ed5134f8e7584de306fb015c1a8d`**, whose original repository CI failed. Separate 6ec core, agentd and Root-fixture results passed; app-server failed. **S0-S5 remain HOLD. Complete physical and historical cost remain unknown (`null`).**

**Observation cutoff: 2026-11-09 11:23:34 UTC.** Quiet-source publication completed with Git/API readback. Workspace-v2 remains pending in Root's scheduling update; no later result is inferred. Common is unchanged.

## Problem and implementation

The common run failed `suite::unified_exec::unified_exec_formats_large_output_summary`. Inspection found two concrete loss paths: lifetime recording owned by a late subscriber, and an extra local broadcast queue before authoritative buffering. **The original CI scheduling cause remains unproven.**

The isolated 45a repair moves the bounded lifetime transcript into `UnifiedExecProcess`. Producers record accepted chunks before exposing them to polling or presentation consumers. Local output consumes the two existing bounded mpsc streams directly, retaining backpressure until both EOFs. Remote normal/recovery paths record newly accepted sequence numbers once. Presentation retains its framing and limits; it no longer owns the transcript.

The manager and terminal summary preserve head/tail bytes, omission counts and exit-versus-EOF semantics without new grace, deadlines, retries or authority. Regressions cover late subscription, prefilled streams through EOF and remote replay after exit. This covers accepted producer bytes, not every upstream transport.

The 6ec child changes only the remote regression's clock oracle: its first version observed 21 ms while requiring exactly 20 ms. It now compares collector completion with an independent timer at the **same original 20 ms deadline**, rejecting early completion and requiring equal observed instants. Production code, output/EOF assertions and the watchdog are unchanged. On 6ec desktop, the three new regressions and original large-output integration case passed within the full core suite.

Published increment008 review files:

- [45a production repair, 25,852 bytes](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/blob/8ca3f19c69f2f14a42aa5fbe3ff72af807c65ff2/qualification/cell_common_candidate/20261108/execution_history/reviewed_changes/core-output-45a-reviewed.patch)
- [6ec reviewed timer patch, 1,651 bytes](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/blob/8ca3f19c69f2f14a42aa5fbe3ff72af807c65ff2/qualification/cell_common_candidate/20261108/execution_history/reviewed_changes/remote-timer-6ec-reviewed.patch)
- [6ec canonical frozen diff, 1,919 bytes](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/blob/8ca3f19c69f2f14a42aa5fbe3ff72af807c65ff2/qualification/cell_common_candidate/20261108/execution_history/reviewed_changes/remote-timer-6ec-frozen.patch)

## Same-source results: 6ec desktop

These rows bind **`6ec5993fec3dcd6a3c569498a1d5b4c277f1c142`**, tree `b0ddbe6b6f83dc42657260b266774f79c9d1ed90`, parent `45a50bffd1631d502889069fc3f713b8a5e775d8`. Parent-source results are not transferred.

| Scope | Actual outcome | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full caller gate | PASS under the original 600-second bound | Source gate, not native cases |
| Strict preparation | All 9 steps returned 0 | V8; ten-helper build/verify; fix and strict Clippy for three owners |
| Full core owning | **3,827 PASS**, 9 original ignored | Four required regressions are a subset; 0 retries or observed LEAK |

| Full workspace v2 | Compiling at the reported cutoff | Original command and 4,200-second budget; no terminal result |
| d274 old-producer control | Prepared, not executed | No counterfactual result yet |

Two managed MCP-review initialization cases and one localhost OAuth callback case remain failed. Passing subsets do not rescue app-server; these failures have not been retried or accepted through relaxed assertions, budgets or security checks.

The workspace fix only makes two optional environment fields nullable in metadata; native environment/command and the original v1 failure remain unchanged.

Core, app-server and agentd retained **4, 6 and 19 native binaries**, respectively, each plus ten helpers, as host-only copies. Core and agentd/Root have independent records readback. All **15,010 source entries** remain unchanged. Retention adds no executions and does not rescue failed tests or claim archived executable bytes.

[Frozen 6ec source](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/tree/6ec5993fec3dcd6a3c569498a1d5b4c277f1c142) was normally published once to `codex/cell-s0-core-output-20261109-898e` for review. Git/API confirmed source, tree and parent; source/index/common/CURRENT were unchanged. Actions reported zero runs at that observation, not CI success. Common/PR-head and scientific acceptance were not promoted.

## Earlier source outcomes remain authoritative

**Common bf42.** The original snapshot has 18 terminal workflows: 12 success, 3 skipped, 3 failure. Full native workspace executed **20,563 selected cases: 20,562 passes and one final failure**, with 139 outside selection and **20,564 actual attempts**. The earlier scoped phase had 7,909 single-attempt passes plus one flaky eventual pass across 7,911 attempts; its 7,910 cases overlap the workspace.

Original Windows logs record **167 selected: 158 clean passes, 8 failures and one body-pass reported LEAK**, without fresh JUnit. A separate five-owner observer ran 11 cases: ten passed and image-edit timed out. Windows is not qualified; legacy FILE_DELETE_CHILD refusals and security assertions remain intact.

**Earlier 3fc (`3fc4725343dccfc9487e937f77e30bc6a5d80dbc`).** Its 2,129 default passes (1,348 app-server; 781 agentd), 2/71 ignored and separate Root parent stay bound to that source. Checkpoint subsets and the initial zero-native dependency failure/recovery are not new 6ec qualification.

**Core repair 45a.** Strict and caller passed; whole core was **FAIL: 3,827 executed = 3,274 PASS + 6 ordinary failures + 545 SIGABRT + 2 TIMEOUT**, with 9 ignored. The four targeted checks had two passes, one ordinary failure and one SIGABRT. **Archiving the run did not change this outcome.** Native, driver and collector failures remain.

All 545 aborts and five ordinary failures contain ENOSPC; the sixth ordinary failure is the timer assertion. The two timeouts are not both attributed to that cause. Later `/tmp` inode exhaustion does not identify an occupying process or make every failure environmental.

**6ec dependency history.** Both AI attempts, including the one authorized recovery, failed fetching the official V8 checksum with HTTP 504: **zero helper, lint, native and negative-control executions**. The original internal preparation return-code field is `null`; overall preparation and V8 returned 1. Desktop later fetched the checksum but hit an artifact failure; explicit recovery verified existing bytes against that fresh checksum. The host/TMPDIR change and old failures remain recorded.

## S0-S5 and real inputs still required

| Stage | Decision | Outstanding acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S0 | HOLD | Ordinary-daemon loop, adoption and distinct successor use |
| S1 | HOLD | Budget-matched gains, error acceptance and retention |
| S2 | HOLD | Prediction/state improve execution and fault handling |
| S3 | HOLD | Benefit over trained baselines including complete cost |
| S4 | HOLD | Benefit over a fixed graph after migration/organisation cost |
| S5 | HOLD | Independent multigeneration, adopted improvements |

Checkpoint transport, FinalUse issuance and Ready/Published mechanisms are real. The Root fixture tests registered HostCAS with a non-root client, conflict, lost acknowledgment and cleanup. It grants no production registration or ordinary-daemon acceptance.

S0 still needs actual I1-I6 inputs: concrete HostAuthority owner; lawful Root seal and non-root identity; activated verifier/roles; five real owner ports; independent signed Generator/Evaluator/Selector/Observer evidence; and effective Published-to-Ready, live-journal and installed-CellBundle consumption by a distinct successor. Fixtures cannot supply missing owners or authority.

## Evidence and cost

[Published increment008](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/tree/8ca3f19c69f2f14a42aa5fbe3ff72af807c65ff2/qualification/cell_common_candidate/20261108/execution_history), commit `8ca3f19c69f2f14a42aa5fbe3ff72af807c65ff2`, contains **87 packets, 10,104 overlapping member entries and 1,348 committed Git files**. These are storage counts. Publication/readback verified four added histories; the previous 83 packets and earlier VERIFY.log omission/correction remain preserved.

Increment008 contains the original 45a failures and 6ec AI dependency failures. **Later desktop recovery, strict/native/Root results and the publication admission above are outside that checkpoint.** Local readback does not mean those bytes are already published.

Formal `qualification/cell-research-stages-20261108/CURRENT_RESULT.json` remains 7,587 bytes, SHA256 `c8b2bbb955272dde7679f86a7f0bf6113c46d7d4fbba3496446399c3615e10e4`. Complete physical and historical cost stay `null`; timings and partial coverage do not establish scientific acceptance.

## What this PR changes

- Assembles the recorded stage/source pins, reviewed HCSN/PQ merge, native API repairs, Matrix 0.19.1 graph and exact vendor backports. The original Matrix 0.18 migration fixture remains intact.
- Recovers terminal training jobs through the original registered Host CAS owner. Uncertain or already claimed jobs are reconciled before another training execution can be admitted.
- Registers the actual ACT1 and async FinalUse callers while preserving grant, fence, goal and recovery ordering. The caller scan retains its original closed set and 600-second CI limit.
- Propagates same-text SDK composition commits through the existing draft owner, including room, draft-limit and rollback checks.
- Makes Guardian reminders and pagination fixtures observe the existing turn-completion fence before persistence and recovery, within their original deadlines.
- Corrects the cold-resume fixture to bind the actual `ThreadItem::SubAgentActivity` event with `SubAgentActivityKind::Started`. It retains the parent thread, turn and call identity, the exact worker path and returned child identity, then waits for that child's completed turn under the original deadline before checking persistence and recovery.
- Reads physical journal bytes through the original locked owners and serialized actor commands. Bounds, CURRENT/health checks, cursor restoration, poisoning and complete byte comparisons remain enforced. Weak observation handles let the runner release its owner before cold recovery.
- Uses the required Windows directory-handle access for the signed-credit ledger fixture and Matrix session parent. Same-handle directory/reparse checks, parent-pin lifetimes, error propagation and original retained-byte assertions remain in place. This API-usage repair does not establish namespace or power-loss durability.
- Repairs canonical-path, socket, peer-lifetime and short-lease fixture setup. The remaining signed-credit fixture now canonicalizes its already-created temporary root before appending the fleet path, retains the TempDir guard and original owners, and reports the caller location when checked fixture setup fails.
- Preserves Windows OpenSSH isolation and executable/input pins while supplying the production ProgramData path from the Windows known-folder API. The operator fixture child commands now receive the OS-derived ProgramData value through the same existing logic; the native oracle and its assertions remain intact.
- Selects the existing supported Elevated mode explicitly in the affected CLI, image-edit and file-approval fixtures. Production legacy-admission refusals and authorization checks remain enforced.
- Builds and publishes the guarded zsh source fix for four actual platforms, then pins the existing consumers and release assembly to the published manifest. Original failures and actual resolver/DotSlash consumption remain recorded.

These changes do not broaden production authorization, weaken signature verification or release live locks to satisfy tests. The original internal deadlines, timeout ceilings and retry budgets remain unchanged.

The isolated 45a repair moves the bounded lifetime transcript into `UnifiedExecProcess`. Producers record accepted chunks before exposing them to polling or presentation consumers. Local output consumes the two existing bounded mpsc streams directly, retaining backpressure until both EOFs. Remote normal/recovery paths record newly accepted sequence numbers once. Presentation retains its framing and limits; it no longer owns the transcript.

The manager and terminal summary preserve head/tail bytes, omission counts and exit-versus-EOF semantics without new grace, deadlines, retries or authority. Regressions cover late subscription, prefilled streams through EOF and remote replay after exit. This covers accepted producer bytes, not every upstream transport.

The 6ec child changes only the remote regression's clock oracle: its first version observed 21 ms while requiring exactly 20 ms. It now compares collector completion with an independent timer at the **same original 20 ms deadline**, rejecting early completion and requiring equal observed instants. Production code, output/EOF assertions and the watchdog are unchanged. On 6ec desktop, the three new regressions and original large-output integration case passed within the full core suite.
